title: Solar Analysis Lab: A browser-based sun path and solar irradiance tool
description:
Solar Analysis Lab is a sun path and solar irradiance tool for architecture students that runs entirely in the browser. It ships as a single self-contained HTML file with no build step for the end user and no install.

The sun is moved through the day and the year over a massing model, with shadows cast in real time and the path drawn in 3D or as a stereographic projection. Geometry can be imported as OBJ, or built from OpenStreetMap buildings over a map basemap or an uploaded site image. Climate is read from an EPW file; with none loaded, a clear-sky model stands in.

A grid of sensors reports solar irradiance in W/m2 and cumulative radiation in kWh/m2 on every surface. The calculation ray traces against a bounding-volume hierarchy in a worker, with the sky discretised over Tregenza/Reinhart patches under the Perez all-weather model, and is validated against the measured global horizontal radiation in the climate file itself. The method notes in docs/method-notes.html document every assumption, name every source the code implements, and declare the tool's limitations.
